title: Serve POST /print-pdf on the agent
description:
Serve POST /print-pdf so a caller that renders a multi-cell label sheet as a PDF can print it through the agent. Today the router serves only /available, /default, /write, /read and /health, and its default arm answers anything else with a plain-text 404.

WHY THIS IS P1 — an investigation run before this repo was split out returned a positive hit: the sheet-PDF path is reachable from a station-attached browser session today and 404s there. The calling page picks its transport solely by probing GET /available, an endpoint this agent does serve, so the caller believes the agent is present and only discovers /print-pdf is missing when the sheet request fails. There is no version negotiation and no build flag anywhere on that path, so nothing gates the attempt.

Single-label ZPL printing is unaffected. Only the multi-cell sheet path is broken, and it fails at the moment an operator tries to print a sheet.
acceptance_criteria: POST /print-pdf accepts a {device, data} body where data is a base64-encoded PDF, spools it to the resolved healthy printer through CUPS WITHOUT -o raw, and answers with the same empty-200 on success / plain-text body on failure convention as /write. The five frozen routes, the Device shape, the CORS origin echo and the X-Print-Agent-Version header are byte-unchanged. A multi-cell sheet print no longer 404s. Covered by a lat.md/tests.md section and a matching // @lat: ref on the Go test.

title: Decide the auto-update story for installed stations
description:
Nothing auto-updates today. A station stays on whatever .pkg an admin last
installed by hand, which is what makes the documented rollback path exactly one
step -- install the previous release's .pkg over the bad build, no uninstall and
no cleanup -- and it is also why a station can silently sit on a build with a
known defect indefinitely.

Decide whether that stays the shipping posture or the agent grows an update
channel, and write the decision down either way. The trade is real in both
directions: an auto-updater on a loopback daemon that operators cannot admin is
a new privileged surface and a new way to break printing unattended, while the
manual path scales with the number of stations and depends on someone noticing.

If the answer is 'stays manual', the deliverable is the rationale plus whatever
makes the manual path observable -- at minimum a way to tell, from GET /health,
that a station is behind.
acceptance_criteria: The decision is recorded in lat.md with its rationale and its rejected alternative. If manual stays, the version-visibility gap is either closed or filed as its own bead. If an update channel is adopted, it does not weaken the Gatekeeper contract: whatever it installs is a notarized, stapled .pkg that would pass spctl --assess --type install with the quarantine bit set.

title: Close the remaining on-station validation items
description:
Close the on-station validation items that automated coverage cannot reach. The Go unit tests stop at a stubbed CUPS: they prove the agent's REACTION to a queue state, never that the state occurs on real hardware.

Proven on a station already: Gatekeeper-clean silent install of a notarized, stapled .pkg; System-keychain cert trust with no authorization dialog and a real label printed over TLS on :9101; unattended RunAtLoad after reboot; a kill -9 respawn in ~3 s; the honest-error direction of failover; and the transport half of a ~540 KB 4x6 job.

Still open, each needing privilege, a GUI, extra hardware, a hand on the cable, or a power-state change:

- failover from a paused USB printer to a network printer — expect 200 plus an explicit fallback log line (needs a second printer)
- unplug/replug across a real USB re-enumeration — the stable uid must survive
- sleep/wake and network-change recovery
- a cold-boot install on a station that has never run the agent
acceptance_criteria: Every open bullet is either observed on a real Apple-Silicon Mac with a real ZD621 and recorded with what was seen, or explicitly deferred in writing with the reason. A uid that changes across replug is recorded as a design finding against stableUID, not closed as a station quirk. A phantom 'Sent' anywhere in the failover half is a hard failure.

title: Define a retention policy for the request and job log
description:
The origin posture is 'auditable rather than silent': every request's Origin is
logged, and every job's outcome is logged with the device uid, byte count, lp
request id and origin. That is the minimal audit trail v1 committed to, and v1
deliberately made a retention policy a non-goal.

The consequence is that ~/Library/Logs/browser-print-agentd/agent.log grows
without bound on a station that prints all day, and the uninstaller deletes it
outright -- which is also the one documented ordering trap, since the log is
most wanted exactly when the agent is being removed because something was
wrong.

Decide what the daemon owns versus what newsyslog or a launchd-adjacent
rotation owns, and whether any field currently logged should not be retained
for the chosen window.
acceptance_criteria: A rotation or retention mechanism is chosen and documented in lat.md, with the size or age bound stated. The audit fields the origin posture depends on -- origin, device uid, byte count, lp request id -- survive within the retention window. The uninstaller's delete-the-log behaviour is either kept with the trap still documented, or changed deliberately.
